record.original_question: Determine whether the border Waring class is contained in the border Chow class; more modestly, prove non-trivial upper bounds for border Waring rank RV(f) in terms of border Chow rank RCh(f).

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Determine whether VWaring ⊆ VChow. More modestly, determine non-trivial upper bounds for RV (f ) in terms of RCh (f ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $f \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_d$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d \ge 1$.

Define the Waring rank $R_V(f)$ to be the minimal integer $r$ such that there exist linear forms $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_1$ with
$$ f = \ell_1^d + \ell_2^d + \cdots + \ell_r^d. $$
Define the Chow rank $R_{Ch}(f)$ to be the minimal integer $s$ such that there exist linear forms $\ell_{i,j} \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_1$ ($1\le i\le s,\,1\le j\le d$) with
$$ f = \sum_{i=1}^{s} \prod_{j=1}^{d} \ell_{i,j}. $$

The border Waring rank $\underline{R}_V(f)$ is the smallest $r$ such that $f$ lies in the Zariski closure of the set of degree-$d$ forms of Waring rank at most $r$; equivalently, the smallest $r$ such that there exist linear forms $\ell_i(\varepsilon)$ depending polynomially on $\varepsilon$ with
$$ f = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \sum_{i=1}^{r} \ell_i(\varepsilon)^d $$
(or, equivalently, $\varepsilon^N f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{r} \ell_i(\varepsilon,x)^d$ modulo $\varepsilon^{N+1}$ for some $N$). The border Chow rank $\underline{R}_{Ch}(f)$ is defined analogously, replacing $d$-th powers $\ell_i^d$ by products $\prod_{j=1}^{d}\ell_{i,j}$.

Let
$$ \mathcal{V}_{\text{Waring}} = \{\,f : \underline{R}_V(f) < \infty \text{ with bound polynomial in the input size}\,\}, \qquad \mathcal{V}_{\text{Chow}} = \{\,f : \underline{R}_{Ch}(f) < \infty \text{ with bound polynomial in the input size}\,\} $$
be the corresponding complexity classes of polynomial sequences with polynomially bounded border Waring rank and border Chow rank, respectively.

(a) Determine whether $\mathcal{V}_{\text{Waring}} \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{\text{Chow}}$.

(b) More modestly, prove non-trivial upper bounds for $\underline{R}_V(f)$ in terms of $\underline{R}_{Ch}(f)$ (or vice versa) for an arbitrary degree-$d$ homogeneous polynomial $f$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on debordering Waring rank (e.g., bounds of the form WR(f) ≤ d·r^{O(√r)} improving earlier d·4^r and d^r bounds) addresses Waring vs border-Waring rank, but does not establish the inclusion of the border Waring class in the border Chow class nor give non-trivial bounds of border Waring rank in terms of border Chow rank. No source found resolves the comparison of these two border-complexity classes, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Improved Debordering of Waring Rank
status_evidence.snippet: If a degree-d homogeneous polynomial f has border Waring rank r, then its Waring rank is bounded by WR(f) ≤ d·r^{O(√r)}, improving prior bounds d·4^r and d^r.
status_evidence.claim: Recent debordering bounds relate Waring rank to border Waring rank but do not address the border Chow rank comparison.

status_evidence.title: De-bordering and Geometric Complexity Theory for Waring rank
status_evidence.snippet: Studies debordering of Waring rank within GCT framework.
status_evidence.claim: Does not establish the inclusion of border Waring class in border Chow class.

status_evidence.title: Taking a Step from the Waring Rank Toward the Chow Rank (Simons talk)
status_evidence.snippet: Talk discussing relationship between Waring and Chow ranks.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the relation between Waring and Chow ranks remains an active research topic.
